articles.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Code, Vision, and Audio
articles.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can jointly process code repositories, visual diagrams, and spoken instructions in a single inference pass. The model demonstrates significant gains on agentic software engineering benchmarks, reportedly resolving 71% of SWE-bench Verified issues autonomously. The release intensifies competition with Google's Gemini Ultra 2 and Anthropic's Claude 4 family, both of which shipped comparable agentic capabilities in recent months.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's RT-4 Robot Foundation Model Enables Zero-Shot Manipulation in Unstructured Environments
articles.summary: DeepMind unveiled RT-4, a vision-language-action model trained on a massive cross-embodiment dataset spanning over 30 robot morphologies. The model achieves zero-shot generalization to novel household manipulation tasks with a 68% first-attempt success rate, a substantial improvement over RT-3's 47%. The work represents a milestone toward general-purpose robotic foundation models that can be deployed without task-specific fine-tuning.

articles.title: Meta Open-Sources Llama 4 with 400B MoE Architecture and 1M Token Context
articles.summary: Meta released Llama 4 under a permissive license, featuring a 400-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture with 32 active experts per forward pass and a native 1-million-token context window. Benchmarks show it competing with proprietary frontier models on reasoning and long-document analysis tasks. The open release has already spawned community fine-tunes optimized for legal, medical, and codebase-scale retrieval-augmented generation workflows.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in Automotive Assembly Lines
articles.summary: Tesla confirmed that its third-generation Optimus humanoid robots have begun performing repetitive pick-and-place and quality inspection tasks across two Fremont assembly sub-lines. The Gen 3 units incorporate improved force-feedback hands with 22 degrees of freedom and on-device vision-language models for defect classification. Tesla says it aims to produce 10,000 units in 2027 for both internal use and commercial sale.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Risk Production of 1.4nm Gate-All-Around Process Node
articles.summary: TSMC announced that its A14 (1.4nm-class) process using gate-all-around nanosheet transistors has entered risk production, with high-volume manufacturing targeted for late 2027. The node promises an 18% speed improvement and 25% power reduction over the N2 node, critical for next-generation AI accelerator and mobile SoC designs. Apple, Nvidia, and Qualcomm are reportedly among the first customers taping out designs on the new process.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Constitutional Steering Vectors for Fine-Grained AI Safety Control
articles.summary: Anthropic published research on 'constitutional steering vectors,' a mechanistic interpretability technique that allows operators to dynamically adjust model behavior along safety-relevant dimensions without retraining. The approach decomposes refusal and compliance behavior into interpretable activation directions, enabling per-deployment calibration of risk tolerance. The technique has been integrated into Claude's enterprise API, giving customers auditable knobs for domain-specific safety policies.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Electric Atlas Platform for Commercial Logistics
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics formally launched the commercial Electric Atlas platform in partnership with Hyundai, targeting warehouse logistics and heavy industrial environments. The humanoid robot features hot-swappable battery modules enabling 6-hour operational cycles and a payload capacity of 25 kg per arm. Pilot deployments with DHL and Hyundai's Kia division are underway, with the companies reporting a 30% throughput increase in mixed palletizing tasks compared to conventional automation.

articles.title: Microsoft and Helion Energy Confirm First Commercial Fusion Electricity Delivery for 2028 Datacenter
articles.summary: Microsoft and Helion Energy announced they have completed key engineering milestones for Polaris, Helion's seventh-generation fusion prototype, clearing the path toward delivering fusion-generated electricity to a Microsoft datacenter in Washington state by 2028. The pulsed field-reversed configuration system has demonstrated sustained net energy gain in lab conditions. If the commercial timeline holds, it would mark the first sale of fusion-generated electricity and a potential inflection point for the energy demands of large-scale AI infrastructure.
